extracted.intended_audience: IP office statisticians, policymakers, researchers, and practitioners working with plant variety and GI statistics
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, metrics and data‑collection conventions used by WIPO to compile and report global plant variety (and related geographical indication) statistics, including definitions (office vs origin), counting rules (equivalent vs absolute), and cautions about comparability and data coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office data vs Origin data
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications received by offices from resident and non-resident applicants are referred to as office data, whereas applications filed by applicants at a national or regional office (resident applications) or at a foreign office (applications abroad) are referred to as origin data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use both views to complement the global picture. Note special treatment for applicants domiciled within EU member states: filing at the CPVO regional office is regarded as a resident filing when discussing office data, and such filings are regarded as regional filings when discussing origin data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident share and Non-resident share (%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resident share (%) reports the proportion of applications (or titles) filed by applicants resident in the jurisdiction; non-resident share (%) reports the remainder filed by foreigners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used throughout tables and figures (e.g., regional resident share, top offices/respective resident/non-resident breakdowns). The report highlights comparisons (e.g., China with 97.4% domestic filings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Growth rate (%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual percentage change in the number of applications, titles issued or varieties in force (e.g., 'Applications Growth rate (%)', 'Titles issued Growth rate (%)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported alongside counts for trend interpretation (figures D1, D2, D15). World totals are WIPO estimates using data covering a specified number of offices (e.g., 74 offices for some series); interpret growth with awareness of coverage and exceptional events (e.g., backlog clearances).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications (absolute count) and Titles issued (absolute count)
rubrics_metrics.description: Raw counts of plant variety applications received and plant variety titles issued by office, origin and year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented by office, origin and region (D1–D17). Explicit caution: 'The procedure for issuing titles varies across offices, and factors such as examination capacity and procedural delays mean there are differences in the time lag between application and title issue dates. For this reason, data on applications for any given year should not be compared with data on titles issued that same year.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant variety titles in force
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of active (in-force) plant variety titles at the end of the year (e.g., 'Around 203,760 plant variety titles were in force at the end of 2024').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported with growth rates and by office. World totals are WIPO estimates using data covering a specified number of offices (e.g., 71 offices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent count vs Absolute count (Equivalent/absolute count ratio)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinction between absolute counts and equivalent counts when regional office filings represent multiple member-state equivalents; an 'equivalent/absolute count ratio' is reported for cross‑border filings and titles abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for applications/titles filed at regional offices (e.g., CPVO) where a single regional filing is equivalent to multiple national filings in member states. See glossary for definition of equivalent applications/titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution decomposition of total growth by resident and non-resident applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Breakdown of total growth rate into the contributions from resident applications and non-resident applications (illustrated in figure D6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps interpret whether growth in an office is driven by domestic or foreign filings. Example explanation: 'applications received by CPVO grew by 14%, with resident applications contributing 11.1 percentage points to total growth and non-resident applications accounting for the other 2.9 percentage points.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional aggregation and coverage notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Totals by geographical region are WIPO estimates using data covering a specified number of offices; each region comprises a stated number of offices (e.g., Africa (8), Asia (12), Europe (35), LAC (14), Northern America (3), Oceania (2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these region definitions when aggregating. The report explicitly notes that world totals are WIPO estimates using data covering 74 offices (or other numbers, varying by series).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection methodology and FTE
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO collects data from offices using a common questionnaire and methodology; FTE (full time equivalent) is used where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every effort made to compile procedural data based on common definitions, but procedural differences remain. Caution is advised when making comparisons across offices. The total number of applications processed for any given office may be incomplete due to omission of elements by the office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of exceptional or non-comparable data (exclusion rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: When anomalies or non-direct application events occur (e.g., titles transferred from EU to UK after withdrawal), such items may be excluded from analysis to ensure accurate comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: UK issued many titles in 2023 related to plant variety rights transferred from the EU; 'Because these titles were not the result of direct applications, they were excluded from the analysis in order to ensure a more accurate comparison between offices.' Apply similar exclusion/annotation rules when reporting anomalies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flags for incomplete, not applicable, or not available data
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of annotation codes in tables: '.. indicates not available', 'n.a. indicates not applicable', footnotes such as '(a) this office did not report data; therefore, applications by origin data may be incomplete.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report such flags clearly in tables and note their implications on totals and rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities examinations only notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Some data series may be limited to formalities examinations only, indicated by a footnote (e.g., '(a) data are for formalities examinations only.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When series are limited to formalities examinations, do not conflate them with full substantive-examination series; annotate accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of standardized figures and tables (D1–D17) as reporting components
rubrics_metrics.description: A defined set of figures and statistical tables (D1–D17) are used to present trends, by office, by origin, by region, and in-force counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the structured outputs (trend charts, top offices/origins lists, contribution breakdowns, tables by office/origin) when compiling or comparing plant variety statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and function of Geographical Indications (GIs)
rubrics_metrics.description: A geographical indication (GI) is a sign identifying a good as having originated in a specific geographical area and possessing a given quality, reputation or other characteristic essentially attributable to its geographical origin. The core function of a GI is to signal a link between the distinct qualities of a product and its place of origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GIs can be protected through various legal means (sui generis, trademark law, regional systems, international agreements). Data collection may be complicated because many countries cannot identify GIs protected through the trademark system; multiple agencies may be involved in GI protection at national level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting rules to minimize double counting of GIs
rubrics_metrics.description: To minimize double counting, GIs in force through the EU regional system and the Lisbon System were counted once only rather than multiplied by the number of member states party to each system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Despite this, the overall total may still include some double counting (e.g., bilateral/plurilateral agreements). The report also provides an alternative total excluding international agreements (around 24,500 GIs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution on comparability due to procedural differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural differences across offices make it extremely difficult to fully harmonize data; 'Caution should therefore be exercised when making comparisons across offices.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysts should not compare raw counts across offices without accounting for differences in procedures, capacity, backlog-clearing efforts, and definitional variations.
